name: Total fat
what_is:
The fat figure covers all the fat in a product: saturated, monounsaturated, polyunsaturated and trans, together in one number.

It is mandatory in virtually every market, and in many it comes with a breakdown of saturates, the subfield regulations treat as most relevant.

The rest of the breakdown — monounsaturated, polyunsaturated — is usually voluntary, so most products do not declare it.

Fat provides 9 kcal per gram, more than twice protein or carbohydrate. That is why it weighs so heavily on the energy figure.
why_botia:
BOTIA flags total fat because the number alone says little: olive oil and lard can declare similar figures, but their composition is very different.

And because front-of-pack thresholds are jurisdiction-specific. A criterion used in one country should not automatically be transferred to another market: the rules, categories and calculation basis can differ.
can_1: Read the declared value and keep its unit and its basis.
can_2: Show whatever breakdown the label declares: saturated, monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, trans.
can_3: Show the reference that applies in the market where the product was labelled, and name the authority that publishes it.
cannot_1: Tell you what percentage of your own needs this value represents.
cannot_2: Work out the type of fat from the total. If the breakdown is not declared, it cannot be known.
cannot_3: Apply one country's front-of-pack threshold to a product labelled in another. The criteria and the bases of calculation differ.
cannot_4: Say that a product with more fat is worse than one with less. It depends on the type of fat, the product and the whole diet.
